description:
Measured on develop 7df703b5f, interp.

  defmodule T do
    @spec g([a], integer) :: integer
    def g(_xs, _n), do: 2
    @spec f([a], (a) -> any) :: integer
    def f(_xs, _g), do: 1
  end

T.g(1..3, 1) is refused: error[spec/violation]: call to g/2 violates its @spec for arguments (%Range{...}, int); the declared domain is ([a0_e], int).
T.f(1..3, fn x -> x end) prints 1. T.f(:atom, fn x -> x end) prints 1 as well. The same holds when the body calls the closure.

So the declared domain of the first argument is not checked at a call whose arguments include a closure. This is why Enum.sort_by, max_by, chunk_by and the other *_by functions accepted a range while declaring [a], and Enum.sum did not.

Not investigated: where the check is skipped, whether it is every arrow-typed parameter or only ones mentioning a type variable, and run/build. Decide the intended behaviour with fz-i89 in view (the user decided there that a spec over an untyped clause follows Elixir and does not narrow); the defect here is that two calls to equally specced functions are treated differently.

Probes: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/b173/spec1.fz .. spec4.fz
title: A call is checked against its @spec when the function also takes a closure
